title: Maneckji Tower of Silence, Yazd (east)
visualBrief: Specific standing eastern/southeastern Maneckji dakhma at Yazd: irregular mapped ring with low damaged roofless masonry and sparse ocher plaster remnants, genuinely open narrow arched passage, bounded supported approach steps, gritty open court, shallow irregular recessed central pit/broken lip and sparse rubble. Four reused shared rubble/raw sandstone/stucco/gravel graphs. No intact historical tall tower, roof, bodies/bones, copied label/photo atlas, lower precinct buildings, the other dakhma, complete hill or broad terrain slab.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Q27702877 identifies the two-tower site, not an invented independent member QID. This independent eastern member is OSMway239508111, matching native circle35184611596943 and its cemetery POI. Use its own anchor54.357023376,31.821894613, heading0/native east-south. Native nineteen-vertex outline fixes the roughly30.44x31.21m base; upper ring is inset0.8m to form the bounded battered rocky contact. Native approach35184755387040 crosses the northeastern rim, giving an internal entrance phase near-0.8rad; fine portal/damage/pit inventory retains20degree/2m approximation. Western Golestan is a separate required member and placement about240m away.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: No qualified mapped building height exists. Surviving inner enclosure nominally1.3..2.5m above the court and1.75m doorway apex are picture-led estimates; shallow pit nominal depth1.0m/radius4.2..4.7m,1.2m masonry thickness, individual broken blocks/plaster fragments and approach allocation are approximate, not an archaeological survey. No restored original exposure-grid or furnished historical scene is invented.

reconstruction.terrainBasis: Keep the original6m standard Mapzen hill, native roads/water and every independent building including the western tower and lower precinct. Replace only this eastern native circle. Court/pit floor is bounded to the mapped circle and seated above occupied coarse-ground maxima; pit remains truly recessed without cutting native ground. A bounded battered raw-stone contact surface within the mapped footprint supports the court above coarse grade; its profile is a visual approximation of the rocky tower seat, not newly surveyed hill terrain. Buried feet and narrow supported stairs meet coarse grade. This visualization contact estimate does not claim a surveyed hill profile, excavation or foundation engineering; no whole-hill mesh, broad slab, ground/water cutout or valley flattening.
